acceptanceCriteria.text: Every existing file and directory under `docs/` is classified as keep, move, rename, merge, archive/history, delete-candidate, or move-out-of-docs, with a reason.
The responsibility-oriented top-level structure is implemented, or any deviation from the proposed structure is explicitly justified in the PR.
`docs/README.md` is the only ordinary Markdown file directly under `docs/` and serves as the documentation entry point.
Each top-level documentation category has an explicit responsibility and placement rule.
All files listed in the migration map are moved/renamed according to the agreed information architecture, unless the PR documents a stronger content-based reason for a different destination.
Existing ADRs remain under `docs/decisions/` with their numbering and history preserved.
Point-in-time dogfood, experiment, and benchmark evidence is separated from current normative documentation.
Historical release documentation is separated from current release operations.
Non-document fixtures under `docs/` are moved out where practical, or their continued presence is explicitly justified.
All Japanese prose in documentation touched by this issue is translated to English.
The repository documents an English-only/default-English policy for documentation and governance prose.
Repository-internal links, README references, scripts, package metadata, CI references, and other path consumers are updated for moved files.
No broken documentation links remain after the migration.
A mechanical check rejects new unclassified files directly under `docs/`, with `docs/README.md` as the intended root-level exception.
The mechanical rule is integrated into the repository's existing governance/CI validation path rather than implemented as an unrelated duplicate authority.
Documentation placement and language rules are discoverable from `docs/README.md` and the repository governance documentation.

issue.title: Reorganize docs information architecture and enforce English-only documentation
